case_name: Mintu Mirdha vs State (Govt. Of Nct Of Delhi)

parties.respondent_defendant: State (Govt. Of NCT Of Delhi), respondent

facts_of_case: FIR registered under Sections 363/366/366A/370A/406/120B of the IPC read with Sections 6 and 17 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012. Applicant seeks bail.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the accused to show that there are material inconsistencies in the statements of the victims.
legal_principles.held: The contentions advanced by Mr Kinger are unpersuasive. First of all, there are two victims in this case and their statements recorded under Section 164 Cr.PC clearly indicate that there are serious allegations against the applicant.

legal_principles.principle: The court should not treat accused at parity with co-accused who have been released on bail without considering the specific allegations against each accused.
legal_principles.held: The contention that the applicant ought to be treated at parity with the other co-accused who have been released on bail is also unpersuasive.

keywords: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
